output.answer: Yes. Ford's most recent layoff action came in September 2026, when it told a works meeting at its Cologne, Germany plant that another 500 employees must leave the company with severance — part of a restructuring launched in late 2025 covering 2,900 Cologne positions, plus 750 more cut in spring 2026 when a vehicle-production shift was eliminated. Earlier in 2026, about 1,600 workers were let go at the BlueOval SK battery plant in Glendale, Kentucky, which Ford is taking over and retooling for energy-storage batteries after dissolving the joint venture in December 2025 (layoffs began February 14, 2026, with a final ~10% delayed to March 31, 2026). That followed Ford's November 2025 announcement of roughly 4,000 job cuts across Europe and the UK. No brand-new layoff announcement was found in November 2026 itself; Ford's restructuring remains active (its own filings project $500M–$1B of 2026 charges 'primarily attributable to employee separations'), and as of early November 2026 some workers at Ford's Oakville, Ontario plant were still being recalled from indefinite layoff.
caveats: No brand-new Ford layoff announcement was found dated November 2026; the most recent confirmed action is the September 22, 2026 Cologne disclosure, and a new announcement after that date cannot be ruled out.
The AP report of 4,000 Europe/UK job cuts carried no publication date on the page retrieved; the timing (November 2025) is inferred from corroborating coverage of the same European restructuring.
The Cologne figures are plant-level and include severance/buyout departures; the Cologne plant's long-term future remains uncertain per the works council, so numbers could change.

The Kentucky BlueOval SK cuts come as the plant transfers from the Ford-SK On joint venture to a Ford subsidiary (Ford Energy), which plans to hire more than 2,100 workers for energy-storage production and is eligible to rehire affected employees — so some jobs may return.

output.question: Has Ford announced layoffs?

key_facts.fact: Ford told a Cologne works meeting that 500 more employees must leave the company with severance under its restructuring program.

The 500 Cologne departures are not additional: they belong to the savings program launched in 2025 covering 2,900 positions, to which another 750 positions were added in spring 2026 when a vehicle-production shift was eliminated.
Ford announced it would cut 4,000 jobs in Europe and the UK, citing disruption from the shift to electric vehicles and economic headwinds.

In December 2025 Ford announced it was dissolving the BlueOval SK joint venture with SK On, retaining the two Kentucky battery plants, and investing $2 billion to retool the operating plant for stationary energy-storage batteries as part of a $19.5 billion redeployment plan.

About 1,600 workers at the BlueOval SK Battery Park in Glendale, Kentucky were let go, with the layoff date around February 14, 2026; roughly 155 employees had their employment extended to at least March 31, 2026 to assist the handover to Ford.

A WARN filing showed the Kentucky battery-plant job cuts affecting around 10% of the remaining workforce were delayed from mid-February to begin March 31, 2026, after about 1,500 workers were already scheduled for redundancy earlier in the year.

Ford's restructuring was still active as of late 2026: its filings project total 2026 charges of $500 million to $1 billion 'primarily attributable to employee separations,' weighted toward Europe; December 2025 actions included cancelling three planned EVs, ending current-generation F-150 Lightning production, and the BlueOval SK JV disposal agreement of December 9, 2025, with about $13.8 billion of Q4 2025 charges.

As of early November 2026, Ford's Oakville, Ontario workforce was still absorbing indefinite layoffs: Unifor Local 707 reported Ford recalling 18 members from indefinite layoff on November 2, 2026, with the most senior member on layoff having a July 2015 seniority date.

Ten months after about 1,500 workers lost jobs at the Hardin County, Kentucky EV battery plant, Ford's new Ford Energy spinoff had begun hiring at the retooled Glendale plant for battery energy-storage production.
